title: JUMUʿAH / FRIDAY
bullets: For one upon whom Jumuʿah is obligatory, the Friday fard is 2 rakʿahs behind the imam after the khutbah, replacing Dhuhr.
4 rakʿahs Sunnah muʾakkadah before Jumuʿah.
4 rakʿahs Sunnah muʾakkadah after Jumuʿah; an additional 2 may also be prayed.
Once the imam begins the khutbah, listen and do not begin voluntary prayer or conversation.
source: Hanafi Jumuʿah rulings; SeekersGuidance Jumuʿah guidance.

title: TARAWIH
bullets: Prayed in Ramadan after Isha and before Witr.
The established Hanafi practice is 20 rakʿahs.
Pray in sets of 2 rakʿahs.
A brief rest after each 4 rakʿahs is traditionally associated with Tarawih.
Congregation for men is recommended; praying alone remains valid.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance: Tarawih 20 rakʿahs.

title: LAYLAT AL-QADR
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
translit: Allāhumma innaka ʿAfuwwun tuḥibbu l-ʿafwa faʿfu ʿannī.
meaning: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me.
bullets: Seek Laylat al-Qadr especially in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan.
Fill the night with salah, Qur'an, dhikr, istighfar, and duʿā.
source: Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 3513; Sahih hadith on seeking Laylat al-Qadr.

title: EID AL-FITR + EID AL-ADHA
bullets: Each Eid prayer is 2 rakʿahs in congregation.
In Hanafi fiqh, the Eid prayer is wajib for those upon whom its conditions apply.
There is no adhan or iqamah for the Eid prayer.
The prayer includes six additional takbirs beyond the ordinary prayer takbirs.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance: method of Eid prayer.

title: EID PRAYER: FIRST RAKʿAH
bullets: Begin with the normal opening takbir and fold the hands.
Recite Thana.
Imam and followers give 3 additional takbirs, raising the hands each time; let the hands fall after the first two and fold after the third.
The imam recites al-Fātiḥah and a surah, then complete ruku and sujud normally.
source: Relied-upon Hanafi Eid method.

title: EID PRAYER: SECOND RAKʿAH
bullets: The imam recites al-Fātiḥah and a surah first.
Then give 3 additional takbirs, raising the hands and letting them fall each time.
On the next takbir, go directly into ruku without raising the hands.
Complete the prayer normally and listen to the khutbah afterward.
source: Relied-upon Hanafi Eid method.

title: JANAZAH: BEFORE THE PRAYER
bullets: The Janazah prayer is performed standing; it has no ruku and no sujud.
Face the qiblah with the deceased placed in front of the congregation.
Intend the funeral prayer and supplication for the deceased.
Follow the imam closely.
source: Hanafi funeral prayer fiqh.

title: JANAZAH: FOUR TAKBIRS
bullets: First takbir: raise the hands, fold them, and recite Thana.
Second takbir: do not raise the hands; recite Salawat Ibrahimiyya.
Third takbir: do not raise the hands; make duʿā for the deceased.
Fourth takbir: do not raise the hands.
End with two salams.
source: Hanafi funeral prayer fiqh; standing and takbirs are core integrals.

title: JANAZAH DUʿA FOR AN ADULT
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِحَيِّنَا وَمَيِّتِنَا، وَشَاهِدِنَا وَغَائِبِنَا، وَصَغِيرِنَا وَكَبِيرِنَا، وَذَكَرِنَا وَأُنْثَانَا، اللَّهُمَّ مَنْ أَحْيَيْتَهُ مِنَّا فَأَحْيِهِ عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ، وَمَنْ تَوَفَّيْتَهُ مِنَّا فَتَوَفَّهُ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ
translit: Allāhumma-ghfir li-ḥayyinā wa mayyitinā, wa shāhidinā wa ghāʾibinā, wa ṣaghīrinā wa kabīrinā, wa dhakarinā wa unthānā. Allāhumma man aḥyaytahu minnā fa-aḥyihi ʿala l-Islām, wa man tawaffaytahu minnā fatawaffahu ʿala l-īmān.
meaning: O Allah, forgive our living and dead, those present and absent, our young and old, our males and females. Whoever You keep alive among us, keep alive upon Islam; whoever You cause to die among us, cause to die upon faith.
source: Sunan Abi Dawud 3201; Jamiʿ at-Tirmidhi 1024.

title: JANAZAH FOR A CHILD
bullets: The Janazah structure is still four takbirs.
After the third takbir, make an appropriate duʿā asking Allah to make the child a source of reward, intercession, and treasure for the parents.
Classical Hanafi books transmit child-specific supplications with variant wording.
Use the wording taught by your imam if he has a preferred Hanafi text.
source: Hanafi funeral prayer manuals; child-specific duʿā wording varies.

title: SOLAR ECLIPSE: SALAT AL-KUSUF
bullets: When a solar eclipse is seen, pray and make duʿā until it ends.
In Hanafi fiqh it is prayed as a two-rakʿah prayer without the multiple rukuʿ structure used in some other schools.
Congregation led by the imam is established for the solar eclipse where possible.
The prayer applies to partial as well as total solar eclipses.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari eclipse hadiths; Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance on partial solar eclipse.

title: LUNAR ECLIPSE
bullets: When a lunar eclipse occurs, turn to Allah with prayer, duʿā, and remembrance.
In the relied-upon Hanafi treatment, the lunar eclipse prayer is performed individually rather than as the special congregational solar-eclipse prayer.
Continue worship while the eclipse lasts.
source: Classical Hanafi distinction between solar and lunar eclipse worship.

title: ISTISQA: ASKING FOR RAIN
bullets: Abu Hanifa’s transmitted position emphasizes repentance, istighfar, and duʿā rather than a special congregational Sunnah prayer.
Abu Yusuf and Muhammad permit a two-rakʿah congregational prayer followed by a sermon.
Later Hanafi verification regards the congregational prayer as recommended based on Prophetic practice.
This is a genuine intra-Hanafi difference and should not be presented as though only one view exists.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance: The Prayer for Seeking Rain.

title: TRAVEL: WHEN QASR APPLIES
bullets: A qualifying journey is roughly the classical travel distance, commonly given around 48 miles / 77 km, with some scholarly estimation differences.
Traveler status begins after leaving the built-up boundary of your home city/town.
If you intend to stay at the destination for 15 days or more, you become a resident there in Hanafi fiqh.
If you intend less than 15 days, traveler rulings remain, subject to home-residence rules.
source: Hanafi travel fiqh; Maraqi al-Falah / Radd al-Muhtar.

title: TRAVEL: QASR PRAYER
bullets: DHUHR
4 fard becomes 2.
ASR
4 fard becomes 2.
ISHA
4 fard becomes 2.
FAJR
remains 2.
MAGHRIB
remains 3.
alert: IN THE HANAFI SCHOOL, A QUALIFYING TRAVELER SHORTENS THE FOUR-RAKʿAH FARD PRAYERS.
source: Hanafi travel fiqh; SeekersGuidance: basic travel rulings.

title: TRAVEL: COMBINING PRAYERS
bullets: The Hanafi school generally does not combine two obligatory prayers into one prayer time during ordinary travel.
Instead, you can use 'apparent combining': pray Dhuhr near the end of its time, then Asr immediately when Asr begins; likewise Maghrib then Isha.
True combining has limited exceptions connected to the Hajj rites at ʿArafah and Muzdalifah.
If following another school for genuine hardship, learn that school’s conditions rather than mixing rulings casually.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance on combining prayers.

title: PRAYER ON A PLANE OR VEHICLE
bullets: For fard prayer, stand, face the qiblah, ruku, and prostrate normally whenever reasonably possible.
If landing or stopping before the prayer time ends is realistically possible, arrange the prayer accordingly.
If genuine necessity prevents normal prayer and the time would otherwise expire, pray according to your actual ability.
Because vehicle/aircraft cases vary, ask your imam about repeating the prayer when you had to omit core conditions.
source: Hanafi travel-prayer principles; case-specific details require qualified review.

title: SICKNESS: PRAY ACCORDING TO ABILITY
bullets: If you can stand for fard prayer without serious harm, standing remains required.
If standing is genuinely impossible or would cause serious pain/harm or delay recovery, sit.
If you can stand only for part of the prayer, stand for what you reasonably can.
If you can make actual ruku and sujud while sitting, do so.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari: 'Pray standing; if unable, sitting…'; Hanafi sick-person fiqh.

title: IF YOU CANNOT MAKE RUKU OR SUJUD
bullets: Pray sitting if possible.
Indicate ruku by bowing the head/body slightly.
Indicate sujud by lowering the head further than for ruku.
Do not lift a pillow or object to the forehead to imitate sujud.
If sitting is impossible, pray lying down using head movements.
source: Hanafi sick-person prayer fiqh.

title: LYING-DOWN PRAYER
bullets: Preferred Hanafi method when unable to sit: lie on the back with the head raised enough that the face is toward the qiblah; bend the knees if reasonably possible.
Alternatively, lie on the side facing the qiblah.
Use a smaller head movement for ruku and a lower movement for sujud.
Do what you genuinely can; Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
source: Hanafi sick-person prayer fiqh; SeekersGuidance on praying lying down.

title: CHAIR PRAYER
bullets: Do not use a chair merely for convenience if you are physically able to perform the required standing and prostration.
If you cannot stand but can prostrate normally, sit on the floor and perform actual sujud where possible.
If you cannot prostrate, you may pray seated with head motions, making the sujud motion lower than ruku.
If you can stand for some portions, perform those portions standing.
source: Hanafi fiqh of praying sitting/chair use.

title: SALAT AL-KHAWF: PRAYER OF FEAR
bullets: The Qur'an gives a special congregational arrangement for obligatory prayer during serious armed danger.
It is not simply a different two-rakʿah prayer to perform whenever you feel anxious.
Its arrangement depends on the actual danger, group, enemy direction, and imam.
In a real emergency, preserve the obligatory prayer according to the rules of ability and follow qualified leadership where available.
source: Qur'an 4:102; Hanafi fiqh of Salat al-Khawf.

title: DUʿA WHEN AFRAID OF PEOPLE
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَجْعَلُكَ فِي نُحُورِهِمْ، وَنَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شُرُورِهِمْ
translit: Allāhumma innā najʿaluka fī nuḥūrihim, wa naʿūdhu bika min shurūrihim.
meaning: O Allah, we place You before them, and we seek refuge in You from their evil.
source: Sunan Abi Dawud 1537.

title: AYAT AL-KURSI • PART 1
arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ، لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ، لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ، مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ، يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ
translit: Allāhu lā ilāha illā Huwa l-Ḥayyu l-Qayyūm. Lā taʾkhudhuhu sinatun wa lā nawm. Lahu mā fi s-samāwāti wa mā fi l-arḍ. Man dha lladhī yashfaʿu ʿindahu illā bi-idhnih. Yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wa mā khalfahum.
meaning: Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. Who can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before and behind them.
source: Qur'an 2:255; Sahih al-Bukhari 2311 on protection before sleep.

title: AYAT AL-KURSI • PART 2
arabic: وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ، وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ، وَلَا يَؤُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا، وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
translit: Wa lā yuḥīṭūna bi-shayʾin min ʿilmihī illā bimā shāʾ. Wasiʿa kursiyyuhu s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ. Wa lā yaʾūduhu ḥifẓuhumā, wa Huwa l-ʿAliyyu l-ʿAẓīm.
meaning: They grasp nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and earth; preserving them does not tire Him. He is the Most High, the Magnificent.
source: Qur'an 2:255; Sahih al-Bukhari 2311 on protection before sleep.
